title: RFP Response Library — Security Question Bank (GTM working sheet)
content:
Purpose
- This sheet is the question bank used to respond to security questionnaires/RFPs with consistent, approved language.
- “Approved answer” text is intended for copy/paste. If a customer asks for contractual commitments, route to Legal + Security/GRC.
- Evidence pointers are INTERNAL and may require NDA + GRC approval before sharing.

How to use
1) Confirm deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) + region.
2) Paste the Approved Answer. Keep the “depends on deployment mode / contract” caveats.
3) If evidence is requested, follow: Confluence → customer-security-review-process (restricted).

Column legend
- Evidence pointer: where to find/share (often restricted). Do NOT forward restricted links to customers.
- Owner: who updates the answer if product reality changes.
- Last reviewed: date the row was last re-validated for external use.

Table (copy/paste friendly)
| ID | Category | Question prompt (customer wording) | Deployment notes (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) | Approved answer (customer-facing) | Evidence pointer (internal) | Owner | Last reviewed | Source of truth |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Compliance | Do you have a SOC 2 report? | Applies primarily to Redwood-operated services; Private is shared responsibility | Yes. Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report covering relevant controls for the hosted service and corporate security program. Access is provided under NDA and via our controlled evidence-sharing process. | Confluence (restricted): compliance-evidence/customer-security-review-process → “SOC 2 access flow”; Evidence index (ENG-23344) | Olga Petrov | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 2 | Compliance | What is the SOC 2 scope / system boundary? | Explain boundary; avoid claiming customer infra is covered in Private | The SOC 2 report describes the control environment and service boundary for Redwood-operated services. Dedicated operated by Redwood is covered to the extent included in the defined system boundary. Private deployments introduce customer-controlled infrastructure and configuration; the shared responsibility model applies. | SOC 2 report (under NDA) + boundary diagram excerpt (request via GRC) | Daniel Carter | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 3 | Compliance | Are you ISO 27001 certified? | Don’t commit; route if asked repeatedly | Redwood maintains a formal security program and third-party assurance (including SOC 2 Type II). If ISO 27001 certification is required, please flag and we will confirm current status and roadmap through the appropriate teams. | Evidence index (ENG-23344): “Certifications snapshot” (if available); otherwise route to GRC | Olga Petrov | 2026-02-19 | Confluence: standard-rfp-response-library |
| 4 | Security testing | Do you perform penetration tests? | Private: depends on customer environment scope | Redwood conducts regular third-party security testing and internal security assessments. High-level summaries can be shared under NDA when available. Remediation and tracking follow our vulnerability management process. | Pen test summary (under NDA) via GRC; Confluence: customer-security-review-process | Marcus Lin | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 5 | Secure SDLC | Do you have a Secure SDLC? | Applies to Redwood engineering org; Private doesn’t change SDLC | Yes. Redwood follows a Secure SDLC including code review, CI/CD guardrails, dependency scanning, secrets management practices, and vulnerability remediation workflows. | Confluence: secure-development-lifecycle-summary | Marcus Lin | 2026-02-18 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 6 | Data use | Do you train on customer prompts/outputs? | Applies across modes; Private is customer-controlled data plane | By default, Redwood does not use customer prompts/outputs to train or fine-tune models. If any optional programs involve use of customer content, they are opt-in and contractually governed. | FAQ v2 section “Data handling”; Contract language (route to Legal for bespoke) | Naomi Feldman | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 7 | Data retention | Do you store prompts and outputs? | Must caveat: depends on mode + configuration; avoid “never” | Redwood processes prompts/outputs to provide the service. Retention of customer content depends on deployment mode and customer configuration. Hosted/Dedicated may retain limited request metadata for billing, abuse prevention, reliability, and support; optional diagnostic logging features may increase what is retained. Private deployments are controlled by the customer within their environment. | Confluence: data-retention-controls-one-pager; Slack thread ref (sales): incident/retention wording | Kevin Osei | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 8 | Data deletion | Can you delete our data upon request? | Private: customer deletes in their env | Redwood supports deletion requests consistent with contract terms and applicable law. For Hosted/Dedicated, deletion applies to data within Redwood-controlled systems and is subject to operational constraints described in our retention/deletion process. For Private, deletion is controlled by the customer within their environment. | Confluence: data-retention-controls-one-pager; Support ticket SUP-19401 notes | Olga Petrov | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 9 | Privacy | Do you sign a DPA? | Typically yes for enterprise; route to Legal for terms | Yes. Redwood supports DPAs for many enterprise customers. Please route the request through the account team so Legal can provide the current approved template and process. | Confluence: (Finance/Legal) DPA process pointers; GRC playbook | Michael Grant | 2026-02-17 | Confluence: standard-rfp-response-library |
| 10 | Subprocessors | Do you have a list of subprocessors? | Hosted uses more subprocessors than Private; confirm current list | Yes. Redwood maintains a list of subprocessors. Subprocessors vary by deployment mode (Hosted typically uses more third parties than Private). We can provide the current list via the approved link/process. | Evidence index (ENG-23344): “Subprocessor list”; if public link exists, confirm latest with GRC | Daniel Carter | 2026-02-19 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 11 | Data residency | Where is our data processed/stored? | Must tie to selected region; call out telemetry/control plane caveat | Data processing location depends on the selected region and deployment mode. Hosted/Dedicated: customers can select from supported cloud regions; data is processed in-region for serving, and certain operational telemetry/control-plane functions may involve cross-region systems depending on configuration. Private: customer controls where systems run and where data resides. | Confluence: data-residency-one-pager | Fatima Noor | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 12 | Data residency | Do you offer EU data residency? | Confirm region availability with SE; don’t overpromise parity | Redwood offers EU-region deployment options for eligible workloads. For exact availability (regions, feature parity, and any constraints), refer to the Data Residency one-pager and confirm current regional support with Solutions Engineering. | Confluence: data-residency-one-pager; Field feedback doc (2026Q1) | Markus Klein | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 13 | Encryption | Is data encrypted in transit? | Applies across modes (Private depends on customer-configured endpoints too) | Yes. Network traffic to the Redwood API and Console is encrypted in transit using industry-standard TLS. | Security FAQ v2; public security overview (docs) link (ENG-23310) | Naomi Feldman | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 14 | Encryption | Is data encrypted at rest? | Hosted/Dedicated: Redwood-controlled systems; Private: customer controls storage | Yes. Data stored within Redwood-controlled systems is encrypted at rest using industry-standard mechanisms provided by our infrastructure and storage layers. Private deployments rely on customer-controlled storage and encryption configuration within their environment. | Security FAQ v2; one-pager pack “Encryption” slide (Drive pack) | Marcus Lin | 2026-02-18 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 15 | Key management | Do you support CMK / customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)? | Must be mode-specific; route if they want a Yes/No checkbox | Options depend on deployment mode. Hosted: Redwood uses managed encryption at rest; customer-managed key options may be available for certain enterprise configurations (confirm scope during solutioning). Dedicated: enterprise configurations can support stronger isolation and additional key management options (confirmed per environment). Private: customers can integrate with their own KMS/HSM and enforce internal key policies. | Confluence: Private deployment notes + solutioning checklist; route to SE + GRC for definitive statement | Colin O'Donnell | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 16 | Auth | Do you support SSO (SAML 2.0)? | Console SSO for enterprise | Yes. Redwood Console supports SSO via SAML 2.0 for enterprise customers. | Confluence: sso-saml-and-scim-one-pager | Ethan Park | 2026-02-18 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 17 | Provisioning | Do you support SCIM? | “May be available” wording; confirm plan/deployment | SCIM support may be available depending on plan and deployment configuration. Please confirm current availability and scope with Solutions Engineering for your target environment. | Confluence: sso-saml-and-scim-one-pager; internal product notes (Auth) | Ethan Park | 2026-02-18 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 18 | Auth | Do you support MFA? | Encourage IdP MFA with SSO | Redwood supports MFA for Redwood-managed accounts and recommends enforcing MFA via your IdP when SSO is enabled. | Confluence: sso-saml-and-scim-one-pager | Kaitlyn Nguyen | 2026-02-18 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 19 | Authorization | Describe your RBAC model. | Provide least-privilege framing; offer matrix reference | Redwood provides role-based access controls in the Console to support least-privilege administration. Roles govern permissions such as user management, API key management, model/deployment configuration, and access to logs/usage analytics. A roles/permissions matrix is available upon request. | Confluence: rbac-model-reference | Ethan Park | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 20 | API security | How are API keys generated/stored/rotated? | Customer responsibility for storage; Redwood supports key mgmt/audit events where supported | API keys are generated and managed via the Console/API with access governed by RBAC. Customers are responsible for securely storing keys in their own systems (e.g., secret managers) and rotating them per their policies. Key events are included in audit logging where supported. | Confluence: RBAC reference + audit logging one-pager | Kevin Osei | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 21 | Audit logging | Do you provide audit logs? | Must state: control plane events; varies by mode | Yes. Redwood provides audit logs for security-relevant actions in the control plane (e.g., authentication/SSO events, user/role changes, key management actions, configuration changes). Coverage varies by deployment mode and configuration. | Confluence: audit-logging-overview-one-pager; Slack (eng-security) audit log scope thread | Kevin Osei | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 22 | Audit logging | Can audit logs be exported to our SIEM? | “Available for enterprise configurations”; confirm destination/format | Export options are available for enterprise configurations. Depending on deployment mode, logs may be exported via supported mechanisms. Please confirm your required destination/format with Solutions Engineering. | Confluence: audit-logging-overview-one-pager; Support ticket SUP-19344 for sample events | Kevin Osei | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 23 | Logging/content | Do you log prompts and outputs? | Must avoid absolute “no”; explain optional diagnostics | Redwood does not require storing prompts/outputs to provide the service; however, optional diagnostic settings and customer configurations may affect what is logged. Redwood recommends minimizing content logging unless needed for debugging and will align configuration to customer requirements when supported. | Confluence: audit-logging-overview-one-pager + data-retention-controls-one-pager | Naomi Feldman | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 24 | Vulnerability mgmt | Do you run vulnerability scanning / dependency scanning? | Applies to Redwood SDLC + infra | Yes. Redwood employs automated scanning and monitoring for dependencies and infrastructure, and uses internal processes for triage and remediation. | Confluence: secure-development-lifecycle-summary | Marcus Lin | 2026-02-18 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 25 | Vulnerability mgmt | What are your remediation SLAs? | Do not commit to specific timelines unless contract; route if needed | Redwood prioritizes remediation based on severity, exploitability, and exposure. Specific timelines are guided by internal policy and may be summarized under NDA. For contractual commitments, please route to Legal and Security/GRC. | Internal vuln mgmt policy (restricted) via GRC; Legal escalation path | Marcus Lin | 2026-02-17 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 26 | Bug bounty | Do you have a bug bounty program? | Don’t speculate; confirm current status | Please confirm current program status with our Security/GRC team. If a program is active, we can provide the official link and scope. | Evidence index (ENG-23344): “Bug bounty status” | Marcus Lin | 2026-02-16 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 27 | Incident response | Do you have an incident response plan? | Applies across modes; for Private, customer also has IR responsibilities | Yes. Redwood maintains an incident response program covering detection, triage, containment, remediation, and post-incident review. | Confluence: incident-response-and-notification-one-pager | Olga Petrov | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 28 | Incident notification | When do you notify customers of security incidents? (e.g., 24/48/72h) | Avoid fixed timelines; contract controls | Redwood notifies customers of confirmed security incidents affecting their data or service in accordance with contractual terms and applicable law.
Approved wording: “Redwood maintains an incident response program and will notify customers of a confirmed security incident affecting the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of the service or customer data in accordance with the parties’ agreement and applicable law.” | Confluence: incident-response-and-notification-one-pager; Slack sales thread (incident wording) | Naomi Feldman | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 29 | Availability | Do you offer an uptime SLA? | Only for eligible enterprise plans; reference executed SLA | Redwood offers SLAs for eligible enterprise plans. SLA terms (measurement, credits, exclusions) are specified in the executed agreement. | Standard order form/SLA template via Legal/RevOps | Jordan Blake | 2026-02-15 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 30 | Support | What are your support hours / response times? | Depends on plan; avoid promising 24x7 unless confirmed | Enterprise support options include business-hours coverage and 24x7 coverage for Sev-1/critical incidents depending on plan. Please confirm the applicable support tier in the executed order form. | Support packaging doc (internal) + account plan | Jasmine Liu | 2026-02-15 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 31 | Private deployment | What does Redwood access in a Private deployment? | Must reflect customer-controlled environment + solution-specific ops | Private deployments are designed to run within customer-controlled environments. Administrative access, telemetry, and support workflows are defined by the deployment architecture and contract. Redwood can support configurations that minimize outbound connectivity and restrict access paths; details are solution-specific. | Private deployment runbook (SE) + solution architecture notes (restricted) | Colin O'Donnell | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 32 | Private deployment | Can Private run air-gapped? | Don’t overpromise; “some configurations” + review required | Some on-prem/regulated configurations can support restricted connectivity patterns. Requirements must be reviewed with Solutions Engineering and Security to ensure operability (updates, monitoring, and support constraints). | SE checklist for regulated deployments; route to Security Eng + SE | Fatima Noor | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 33 | Shared responsibility | Who is responsible for patching/infrastructure security in Private? | Customer controls infra; Redwood controls Redwood-delivered components | Customers are responsible for securing and patching their underlying infrastructure and enforcing environment controls. Redwood is responsible for the security of Redwood-delivered components and for providing guidance on secure configuration. | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 (Private section); SE boundary statement | Vivek Kulkarni | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: enterprise-security-faq-v2 |
| 34 | Data flow | Can you provide a data flow diagram? | Mode-specific; share safe diagram or under NDA | We can provide deployment-appropriate architecture and data flow information as part of the security review process. For detailed diagrams, we may require an NDA depending on content. | Evidence process + approved diagrams folder (restricted) | Daniel Carter | 2026-02-19 | Confluence: customer-security-review-process |
| 35 | Auditability | Do you log admin actions (user changes, key creation, config changes)? | This is the “audit logs” scope; avoid promising every event | Redwood audit logs capture security-relevant control-plane actions such as authentication/SSO events, user/role changes, key management actions, and configuration changes. Exact event coverage depends on deployment mode and configuration. | Confluence: audit-logging-overview-one-pager (event categories) | Kevin Osei | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: audit-logging-overview-one-pager |
| 36 | Data retention | What are your retention defaults? Can we configure retention? | Must refer to one-pager; varies | Retention defaults and configurable retention controls (where available) are documented in our Data Retention Controls one-pager. We can align configuration to requirements depending on deployment mode and plan. | Confluence: data-retention-controls-one-pager | Kevin Osei | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: data-retention-controls-one-pager |
| 37 | Data residency | Can you guarantee all data stays in-region (no cross-region)? | Don’t guarantee; explain “may involve” and route | Redwood supports region selection for serving. Depending on configuration, some operational telemetry and control-plane functions may involve cross-region systems. If strict in-region-only requirements apply, please flag so Solutions Engineering and Security/GRC can confirm feasibility for the proposed deployment. | Confluence: data-residency-one-pager; route to SE | Markus Klein | 2026-02-20 | Confluence: data-residency-one-pager |
| 38 | Legal/commercial | Will you sign our security addendum / provide security appendix redlines? | Route to Legal; don’t ad-lib | Please route the requested language through the account team. Redwood’s Legal and Security/GRC teams review and approve customer-facing security commitments and redlines through the standard intake process. | Confluence: security-appendix-requests-intake | Michael Grant | 2026-02-16 | Confluence: security-appendix-requests-intake |

Backlog / TODO (not yet standardized)
- BCDR/DR (RTO/RPO) language: needs alignment with SRE + support tiers (owner: Naomi Feldman)
- Data classification / HIPAA posture wording for regulated prospects: create mode-specific safe language (owner: Fatima Noor)
- “Status page URL” and customer comms workflow: confirm official link + comms template (owner: Jasmine Liu)

Notes to self (for maintainers)
- If you edit any “Approved answer” cell, update last reviewed + ping #sales and #eng-security for validation.
- When in doubt, prefer the Confluence canonical pages; this Drive sheet is a working artifact for field copy/paste.
